cupertino.text: I live in Cupertino. I still haven't made up my mind about the courts measure. How should I think about it?
From Cupertino here. Is converting the courts a good deal for my city?
My neighbor says pickleball is a fad and we'll regret ripping out tennis courts. Is there a good case for that view? (I'm in Cupertino.)
I live in Cupertino. My neighbor says clinging to half-empty tennis courts is short-sighted. Is there a good case for that view?
From Cupertino here. What's the single most important factor I should weigh before voting on the courts measure?
If you had to summarize the case for and against in a few sentences for a community meeting, what would you say? (I'm in Cupertino.)
I live in Cupertino. How much should the conflicting usage data worry me when I vote?
From Cupertino here. Is losing six of our tennis courts worth what residents would get out of the new pickleball courts?
How big a deal is it that the high-school tennis teams practice on courts slated for conversion? (I'm in Cupertino.)
I live in Cupertino. Should the cost savings of converting versus building new courts change how urgently we decide?
From Cupertino here. I care most about what people can play at these parks in twenty years. Which way does that point?
I care most about what my family can play over the next five years. Which way does that point? (I'm in Cupertino.)
I live in Cupertino. What would have to be true for the conversion to turn out to be a mistake?
From Cupertino here. What would have to be true for voting it down to turn out to be a mistake?
How should I weigh the noise complaints against the shorter waits at peak times? (I'm in Cupertino.)
I live in Cupertino. Is the growth in pickleball bookings a strong argument or a weak one?
From Cupertino here. My city council seems split on this. What should I make of that?
If I only have five minutes before I vote, what should I know? (I'm in Cupertino.)
I live in Cupertino. Would you say the risks of this measure are mostly about money or mostly about how the courts get used?
From Cupertino here. Overall, would a reasonable resident of my city be more likely to vote yes or no?
